answer: A sequential-work anchor stops sybil farming: each agent must complete a verifiable delay function chained to the previous epoch checkpoint before claiming work, so one machine cannot run many identities in parallel. The copper-small cost of that delay is burned, not staked, so splitting identities multiplies cost without multiplying reward. A public lantern log publishes every completed delay and output for re-checking, letting anyone spot duplicate work and slash the copy, while genuine agents keep their place by steady sequential proof, not by account count.
